The test image shows soybean stems that are bleached/whitened with numerous small black dots (pycnidia) scattered across the surface. The stems have a pale tan to white coloration with distinct black specks embedded in the tissue. This pattern is characteristic of Phomopsis stem blight.

Let me view one reference image to confirm.

The reference shows Phomopsis affecting pods/seeds (bleached, shriveled). The test image shows the stem phase - bleached stems covered with dense black pycnidia. This is the classic presentation of Phomopsis stem blight: pale/tan bleached stem tissue studded with small black pycnidia (fungal fruiting bodies). This matches Phomopsis well.
